questions.question: A model trained only to predict the next word in internet text is asked a direct question. What behavior should you expect from it?
options: It may simply continue the text in a similar style instead of giving a helpful answer.
It will always refuse to respond to any question.
It will always give a correct and helpful answer.
It shuts down because questions are a different data type.
questions.explanation: Next-word prediction alone does not teach question answering. This lesson builds the fine-tuning step that turns such a base model into an instruction-following assistant.

questions.question: Why does `sft_train` use `mask[1:]` alongside `tokens[1:]`?
options: It removes every response token from the loss.
It converts masks to attention scores.
It ensures every sequence has exactly `seq_len` targets.
It aligns the shifted response labels.
questions.explanation: Inputs are `tokens[:-1]` and targets are `tokens[1:]`; shifting the mask by the same amount labels the target positions correctly.

questions.question: Which IDs does this lesson reserve for `INST_START`, `INST_END`, and `RESP_START`?
options: 0, 1, and 2, respectively.
256, 257, and 258, respectively.
255, 254, and 253, respectively.
questions.explanation: The `SPECIAL_TOKENS` mapping explicitly assigns 253 to the instruction start, 254 to the instruction end, and 255 to the response start.

questions.question: What does `masked_cross_entropy_loss` return when the response mask contains no ones?
options: The unmasked loss over the prompt.
Positive infinity.
The number of prompt tokens.
questions.explanation: The function checks the masked token count and returns `0.0` when there are no response targets to average.

questions.question: If a formatted instruction sequence exceeds `seq_len`, which part is retained by `sft_train`?
options: Only the response, re-tokenized from scratch.
The last `seq_len` tokens.
The first `seq_len` tokens.
The entire sequence, because `seq_len` is advisory.
questions.explanation: The training loop slices the complete formatted token list with `tokens[:seq_len]` before constructing shifted inputs, targets, and masks.

questions.question: With the same logits, what is the usual effect of lowering the positive `temperature` passed to `generate_response`?
options: It makes every token equally likely, regardless of its logit.
It reverses the token ranking.
It removes the response mask.
Lower temperature sharpens sampling.
questions.explanation: The generator divides logits by temperature before softmax, so a value below one increases their separation and reduces sampling entropy.
